about: Masts, tops, caps, yards, booms, bowsprit and jibbooms for the frigate Commonwealth (docs/shipkit-3), read by Tools/shipkit/frigate/spars.py. Lengths in feet, diameters in inches. Each number says where it comes from: 'list' is the War Office's statement of 31 March 1795 of masts and yards for the 44-gun frigates 'according to Mr. Steel's method'; '1801' the Navy's December 1801 orders for the 44s (fore 95 ft x 32 in, main 105 x 35, mizzen 92 x 24, bowsprit 64 x 34; quoted in T. Martin, 'Constitution Close Up', USS Constitution Museum), kept as the cross-check; '36s' scaled from the War Office's 1794 list for the 36-gun frigates (topmasts and topgallant masts there 'will answer for both'); 'rule' a proportion of the period (David Steel, 'Elements and Practice of Rigging and Seamanship', 1794, as modelling references quote it: not checked against the book here, whose transcriptions this session cannot reach); 'draught' read off the 1817 sail plan 'A Draft of the U.S. Frigate Constitution' (NARA 102278445, refs.json) at 10.31 px/ft both ways (its deadeyes are round), 'by eye' sized to look right where nothing says.

sources.list: https://wardepartmentpapers.org/document/78108/ (statement of lengths of masts and yards of 44-gun frigates; read through search transcriptions)
sources.36s: https://wardepartmentpapers.org/document/47336/ (dimensions of masts, yards and spars for 44 and 36 gun frigates, 1794)

registration.note: the 1817 draught against the model (docs/shipkit-3): draught x = 0.9292 ship x px + 337.1 (from its gun ports B..O against the model's 1..14, 10.31 px/ft), draught y = 2302.3 + 0.00924 draught x - 10.31 z ft (the load line at z = 0, a 0.53 deg tilt of the sheet). Its hull is drawn about 16% deeper than the 1927 lines (11.95 px/ft up the side), so heights near the hull are read against the hull and the rig's against the waterline

step.note: the lower masts step on the keelson: keel, floors and keelson about 3 ft over the rabbet (the hold slice builds them)

fore.x_note: draught: the mast's centre just above the rail (draught x 2349.6); the rake by eye from the draught (it stands nearly upright)

lower.src: rule: 8/9 of the main mast (1801: 95 x 32); 1 in of diameter a yard of length; the head 5 in a yard

fore.yard_src: draught: the fore yard 9.7 ft under the top

top.src: draught (fore and aft); breadth 4/3 of that (rule)

topmast.src: 36s: 0.9 of the main topmast; 1 in a yard; head 5 in a yard

topgallant.src: 36s scaled (42 ft with the royal pole, 15 ft of it the pole, on a 36); 1 in a yard of the mast to its stop

main.x_note: draught: 1527 above the rail, 1512 at the masthead (1.2-1.5 deg aft)

lower.src: list: 109 1/6 ft, half the gun deck plus the extreme breadth (1801: 105 x 35); 1 in a yard; head 5 in a yard

main.yard_src: draught: the main yard 10.4 ft under the top

top.src: draught (fore and aft); breadth 4/3 of that (rule). The rule's 1/3 of the topmast (21.8 ft) is wider than the draught's tops: theirs is used

topmast.src: list: 65 1/2 ft, 3/5 of the main mast; 1 in a yard; head 5 in a yard (draught 9.9 ft)

topgallant.src: 36s scaled (44 ft with the pole on a 36); 1 in a yard of the mast to its stop

mizzen.x_note: draught: 974 above the rail; it rakes aft more than the main (by eye)
mizzen.yard_src: the main's proportion of the head (the draught hangs the crossjack 5.8 ft under the top, where the gaff's jaws would meet it)

lower.src: rule: 6/7 of the main mast (1801: 92 x 24); 3/4 in a yard; head 5 in a yard

top.src: draught (fore and aft); breadth 4/3 of that (rule)

topmast.src: 36s: 3/4 of the main topmast; 1 in a yard; head 5 in a yard

yards.note: length overall, diameter at the slings, and each yardarm (outside the stop cleats). The yardarms by rule: 1/20 of the length for the lower yards, 1/9 for topsail yards (the reef earings), 1/12 above. Royals 2/3 of the topgallant yards (rule); the 1795 list stops at the topgallants

main_yard.src: list (Asa Curtis gives the United States 95 ft)

mizzen_topgallant_yard.src: rule: 0.6 of the topsail yard, as the list's main and fore

yards.diam_note: 5/7 in of diameter a yard of length (rule)

studding_sail_booms.note: on the fore and main lower and topsail yards, in boom irons, half the yard long, 1 in of diameter for each 5 ft (rule)

bowsprit.src: list: 65 1/2 ft (1801: 64 x 34); its diameter the 1801 ratio to the main mast
bowsprit.line: its heel stands on the forecastle deck, placed so the cap at its end lands on the 1817 draught's cap (3048, 1912): that puts the heel about 16 ft inside the stem (the Navy's 1849 spar deck plan, NARA 75841368, draws a later bowsprit's heel there, 10 ft inside the stem; the gun deck plan has none). The steeve is the draught's (its edges between draught x 2730 and 3000). It passes out over the stem head, which is cut down to bed it (spars.Rig.stem_bed, skin.Skin.backbone); the knightheads beside it and the opening in the bow's bulwark are slice 9's

jibboom.src: rule: 5/7 of the bowsprit, 1 in a yard; draught: its end 29 ft past the cap

flying_jibboom.src: draught: its end 20 ft past the jibboom's; new in the 1790s

spritsail_yard.src: rule: the fore topsail yard's length; slung under the bowsprit 0.78 of the way out

boom.src: draught: from the mizzen to its end over the stern 65 ft, rising aft, its jaws about 2 ft over the quarterdeck rail (so it swings over the rail and the taffrail); its diameter by eye

gaff.src: draught: its jaws 4.8 ft under the mizzen top, its peak 52.3 ft aft and 18.3 ft up

spanker.brace_note: the boom and gaff swing 40 deg either way: about where the after mizzen shrouds (slice 4) stop them

taper.note: diameter along a spar as a fraction of its greatest (rule). Masts by quarters from the partners or cap up to the hounds; yards by quarters from the slings out to the yardarm's end

fittings.note: fractions of the lower mast's diameter D unless named; by eye from period drawings and the draught

head_gap_in.note: between a masthead's fore face and the next mast's heel, in inches: the stays come down the masthead's fore face from their eyes, in front of the shrouds' eyes, and turn forward under the heel (slice 4), so the gap is a shroud eye and a stay across, and an inch: lower masts 3.3 + 5.6 in (fore and main) and 1.9 + 2.7 in (mizzen), topmasts 2.2 + 3.2 in and 1.4 + 1.8 in (standing_1797.json's sizes). The caps' bridges between their two holes are as broad

lubber_hole_in.note: the lubber's hole's sides stand this far off the trestletrees' outer faces: the lower shrouds' legs (slice 4) come down through the hole, and this leaves them about an inch clear of the hole's coaming (0.8 to 1.0 in). Slice 3 had 4.2 in, which put the legs through the coaming

cheek.note: the lower mast's cheeks stop 0.4 ft above the lower yard (never longer than 0.55 of the head), so a braced yard swings clear of them; the topmast's are 0.35 of its head and the topsail yard hoists to 0.4 ft under them

hoops.note: iron hoops on the made lower masts and the bowsprit

paint.note: 1797: masts, topmasts, booms and bowsprit bright (oiled pine); mastheads, tops, caps, crosstrees and all yards black; iron black

draught_heights.note: heights read off the draught (z ft over the load line at 10.31 px/ft) for rig_check.py: [draught x, draught y]. The 1817 rig carries a skysail yard above each royal (draught y 307 fore, 153 main, 487 mizzen) on a pole up to the truck, so its trucks stand a skysail pole higher than the model's royal poles
